Choose New Game, pick a character and choose a level. Each character brings their own starting cards and packs. Press Start Run.
Open each booster and reveal its cards. These cards join your collection for this run. You do not have to choose just one card from a pack.

Tap cards to add or remove them. Start with at least 20 Main Deck cards. Each boss you beat raises the minimum by 10, up to 40. Relics can also change the minimum. You can use up to 3 copies of the same card. Fusion monsters go in the Extra Deck. Hold a card to read it. Your starting signature cards can be removed too.
When your deck is ready, use the arrow to pick your next opponent. Check the reward shown with each opponent before choosing.
After a duel, the tally shows how many coins you earned. Winning quickly gives a bonus. Very long duels earn less from later actions.

Tap a slot to spin for a random card. A reroll costs 15 coins every time. Each slot can be rerolled on its own. Extra-card relics add more slots; bosses give 5 before relic bonuses. Press Confirm when you are happy.

Select the items you want, then press Buy. Cards and opened packs join your run collection; use Edit deck to put them in your deck. Relics work as soon as you buy them. The shop also has a reroll button with its price shown.
The reward shown on an opponent adds matching cards and a booster to the next shop. It is extra shop stock, so you still pay for it. When you are ready, use Next Duel.
Relics change the rules for your run. They can boost cards, heal you or change rewards. You can buy them in the shop. Open Relics to read what you own. The easiest level has no relics.

After a boss, choose 1 of 3 cursed relics. Each has a benefit and a drawback. You get one reroll of the choices. The relic stays with you for the run, so read both parts before picking. This choice is skipped on the easiest level.

Every third duel is a boss. Read its curses before you start. A curse is like a relic for that encounter: it changes the rules and can make the fight harder. Boss curses apply to that fight; a cursed relic you take afterwards stays with your run.

After 9 wins, you can challenge the World Champion. Beat that extra opponent to start another loop. After completing your second loop, Obelisk the Tormenter becomes the required opponent to start further loops. You keep your cards, coins and relics. Later loops use stronger Tier 4 and fallen Ultimate Collector opponents. Each new loop adds 100 enemy ATK/DEF and 2,000 enemy LP.

Pick a character and host or join a room. Share the room code with your friend. You play a run together against the CPU, taking turns in duels. Open packs, build your decks and use the shop between fights.

Choose a character, then host or join. Once both players are connected and ready, you each open double the normal starting boosters and keep the character’s signature cards. Build 40–60 Main Deck cards and press Ready. Play a best-of-three match. No siding or banned/limited list, but the 3-copy limit still applies. Decks are shuffled each duel. Reopen Draft Duels after a disconnect to try to return to your room.

Import a saved singleplayer run and name your collector. Importing moves it out of singleplayer. Build a 40–60-card Main Deck using this mode’s card limits. Host or join a best-of-three match, with side decking between duels. The winner takes 5 cards from the opponent. Losing the match permanently deletes that collector. Your other saves are safe.
Track the cards you have found

Collection shows the game’s cards, packs and relics. Search or filter to find something, then tap it for details. Cards you have owned in singleplayer or Ultimate Collector get a colored frame. Use Registered to see cards you have found and Missing to see what is left. This does not give those cards to every run.
The tabs also show Run History, Device Stats, Global Stats, Ultimate Collectors and Achievements. Pick a tab to browse it.

Open Settings and press Upload Replays. The latest 100 duels are kept on your device. Uploads need internet. Replays show the decks, decisions and results, so we can compare player choices with the CPU and improve how it plays.
During a singleplayer duel, open Options, then Flag behaviour. Say what the CPU did and what you expected. The game attaches the replay up to that moment. Send unsent flags when you are back online.
Open Settings, then Link Devices. Create a code on one device and enter it on the other within 10 minutes. This shares unlocks; it does not move your active runs or Ultimate Collectors.

While you play online, saves are backed up in the background. In Settings, open Recover Save Data and keep a copy of your backup code. If you lose progress, contact the admin on Discord. They can give you a recovery file to load here.
Settings lets you change music and sound volume. Turn on Simple Backgrounds for static colors and lower battery use.

Tap a card to preview it; hold it to open its details. An inspection window pauses the CPU until you close it. The Chain button cycles through Chain, No chain and Chain sometimes. Sometimes asks at summons, attacks and card activations. Options also has a Log: tap an action to inspect its cards.
Use the Discord icon on the main menu to report bugs or suggest deck changes. Include what happened and a screenshot or replay when possible.
